summary: Yasuo Yuasa (1925–2005) was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied under Tetsuro Watsuji and at the University of Tokyo. His career included posts at Tokyo, Yamanashi, Osaka, Tsukuba (1981–1989), and J. F. Oberlin University.

Yasuro Abe (b. 1953) is a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied at Wako and Otani universities. He held academic posts at Osaka, Otemae, Nagoya (1994–2019), Nichibunken, Ryukoku University, ICPBS, and IIBS.
Yasusaburo Sakaki (1870–1929) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1891–1895), later holding posts there (~1898–1906) and at Kyushu University (~1906–1925).

Yasutaka Muroya is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He has been affiliated as a project research associate at the University of Vienna (attested 2007) and Leipzig University (attested 2015), and at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.

Yasutoshi Murakami (b. 1941) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Tohoku University. He held positions at Yamaguchi University, Koyasan University (~1989–2007), and served as president of the Association of Esoteric Buddhist Studies.
Yawen Yang is a scholar in Buddhist studies. Yang studied at Fo Guang University, completing an MA under the supervision of Yongdong Shi (attested 2009).

Yeshe Thubten (1935–1984) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Sera Monastery under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Trijang Rinpoche, Geshe Rabten, and Zong Rinpoche. He founded several Buddhist organizations and taught at UC Santa Cruz (1977–1978).

Yeshi Dhonden (1927–2019) worked in Tibetology and traditional medicine. He studied under Khyenrab Norbu at the Chakpori Institute of Tibetan Medicine, and later founded Men-Tsee-Khang in 1961, serving as its director until 1966.
Yi-hsun Huang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. Huang earned a PhD at the University of Virginia, studying under doctoral supervisor Paul Groner.

Yifa (b. 1959) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at National Taiwan University, University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and Yale University under Stanley Weinstein. She held posts at University of the West, Harvard University, and founded the Woodenfish Foundation.
Yifan Zhang is a scholar in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. Affiliated with Ghent University (attested 2026), Zhang has been both a PhD student and a faculty member there.

Yigal Bronner is an Indologist who studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and under Sheldon Pollock at the University of Chicago (~1994–1999). He later served as an associate professor at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~2008).

Yiliang Zhou (1913–2001) worked in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He studied at Fu Jen, Yenching, and Harvard universities, as well as under Yinke Chen, and served as a professor at Peking University (~1952–2001).
Ying-Kuang Chu (1883–1973) was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He pursued traditional studies under teachers Nona Hutuktu and Gangkar Rinpoche.

Ying-shih Yü (1930–2021) was a sinologist and historian educated at Yenching, New Asia College, and Harvard. He held major posts at Michigan, Harvard, New Asia College, Chinese University of Hong Kong, Yale (1977–1987), and Princeton (1987–2001).

Yingguang Qu (1883–1973) was active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Hangzhou Chicheng Public School (~1905–1907) and under traditional teachers Nordan Hutuktu (1926) and Puren Bai (1929).

Yingshan Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. Chen served as a professor (attested 1996) and later as an honorary research fellow (retired February 2023) at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies.

Yinke Chen (1890–1969) was a historian, sinologist, and linguist who studied widely, including at Berlin, Zurich, Sciences Po, and Harvard under Lanman, Lüders, and Müller. He held professorships at Tsinghua, Peking, National Southwestern Associated, Yenching, and Sun Yat-sen universities.

Yinshun (1906–2005) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Taixu and earned a doctorate from Taisho University. He taught at the Minnan and Wuchang Buddhist Institutes and held leadership posts at Shandao Temple and the Hong Kong Buddhist Association.
Yirmiyahu Yovel (1935–2018) was a scholar of philosophy. He pursued his education at Hebrew Reali School, the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1957–1968), and Princeton University (~1966–1968).
